children: As barc ratings Remain suspended... Javed Farooqui Mumbai: The ministry on information and broadcasting's (MIB) new TV ratings policy has paved the way for cable and DTH operators to publish their own viewership data, potentially reshaping audience measurement as Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) ratings remain suspended.

GTPL Hathway has moved first by publishing data of RPD-based service, but industry-wide adoption faces hurdles over scale, sampling and credibility. RPD captures viewing information from connected set-top boxes (STBs), tracking which channels households watch and for how long. Unlike BARC's panel-based system, which uses people meters and household-member information to estimate individual viewing, RPD typically records viewing at the household or device level.

Its industry-wide relevance will depend on scale, geographical representation and methodological transparency. GTPL is tracking viewing through 10,000 STBs and plans to expand to 50,000, working with TAM India to generate the data. Tata Play has also used RPD for years, primarily for internal content planning, according to industry sources. BARC earlier piloted RPD with Airtel Digital TV and DEN Networks, but the initiative failed to scale as operators sought compensation for sharing data and costs proved prohibitive.

BARC has not published ratings since June, after the ministry of information and broadcasting asked it to comply with the TV Ratings Policy 2026. Registration applications from BARC and TAM remain pending. The renewed interest in RPD also follows a 2021 recommendation by an MIB-appointed committee to make it a mandatory capability in future STBs deployed by distribution platform operators (DPOs).

Partho Dasgupta, managing partner at Thoth Advisors and former CEO of BARC India, said more DTH and IPTV operators should explore RPD. It could give rankings within an operator's territory, but cannot serve as the industry's trading currency because individual-level and demographic cuts are unavailable. Sampling and measurement methodologies would also need scrutiny to establish whether data represents India's wider TV audience, he said.

title: Centre Allows TV Operators to Publish Own Viewership Data
